chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Pops Smith's long career and late-life Tenderly
summary: Pops, the best of the brothers, played first trumpet with Fletcher for years, retired with Calloway at 66 and played beautifully into his eighties.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Pops to me was the greatest of the three. He played first trumpet with Fletcher for years and years and years and years. He played -- he come in the band before Don left the band to go to McKinney. So Don left the band in '27. So Pops had to be there in '27, you know.
Wow. I know he was in Cab Calloway's band but he retired from playing in Cab Calloway's band. I
remember he was 66 years old then.
Oh, yeah. We celebrated his birthday, remember?
That's right. You sure do have a great memory. That's marvelous.

Yes, we did. Yes, we celebrated his birthday. And do you know still, before he died, he was out in California and the guys told me that I think, I forget the trumpet player's name offhand told Pop let me hear him play. So Pop said all right. He said, "I'll play a little "Tenderly," and took his horn out there and played"Tenderly" so pretty it'd make you sick. And that was when he was -- just before he died. He had to be in his eighties.
You know? And he said, "Son, this is the way it's supposed to go."
